transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep forgetting things I’m supposed to do—scheduled callbacks, work orders, even basic follow-ups I told people I’d handle. It’s gotten piled up at work, and they sent me here before it costs me my chance at moving up.
Have you had trouble paying attention or staying organized since you were a child?

Yes. I remember being like this back in grade school, way before any job pressure. Teachers would say I was bright, but I was always losing papers, missing parts of directions, and needing reminders to finish my classwork.
Do these problems with forgetfulness and staying organized happen in other parts of your life too, not just at work?

Yes, it does. It’s not just work, though work is where it’s gotten me in trouble. I’ll forget callbacks I said I’d make, work orders I’m supposed to handle, and follow-ups I promised people. Then it piles up, and I don’t catch it until someone else points it out or it’s already become a problem. That’s basically what got me sent here.
Do you often act impulsively, like speaking or doing things before thinking them through?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed that as a big thing for me. I mean, I might say something without thinking once in a while like anyone, but that’s not what I’d say is the main problem.
Have these attention and forgetfulness problems caused problems in your home life?

It affects home some, but honestly the worst of it has become work. I’ve got a backlog now, tenants complaining, and there’s a safety review on my record. I’m really worried it’s going to ruin the promotion track I’ve been trying to work toward.
Do you often feel anxious or worried a lot?
I mean, I worry about things, sure, especially when something’s going wrong. But I don’t know if I’d say I’m anxious all the time. It’s not something I’ve really thought of as the main issue.
Do you have the same trouble paying attention when you’re not at work?

Yeah, it happens outside of work too. Like if I’m trying to read something on my phone or go through a set of instructions, I’ll start off thinking I’m following it, and then halfway through my mind’s already jumped to some other sound or something else I need to do. Then I realize I don’t actually know what I just read.
Are you often easily distracted by things going on around you?

Yes, pretty often. I’ll start a digital work order thinking I’ve got it, and then halfway through the notes my mind just slips off—like to a noise nearby or the next job I’m thinking about. Then I look back and realize I don’t really know what I just read.
Have there been any periods in your life when these attention and forgetfulness problems were not a problem for you?

Not really, no. I can remember being like this way back in grade school, before work or any of this pressure. Teachers would say I was bright, but I was always losing papers, missing parts of the directions, or needing reminders to finish my classwork.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent pattern of inattention beginning in grade school and continuing into adulthood across multiple settings. Confirmed symptoms include forgetfulness, disorganization, losing papers, missing parts of directions, needing reminders to finish tasks, difficulty sustaining attention while reading or processing instructions, and easy distractibility. These symptoms are causing clear occupational impairment. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms were not prominent, supporting predominantly inattentive ADHD.
